subject: Aligning log retirement windows & DPA subprocessor transfer clause
messages:
From: Sara Cole <sara.cole@medilink.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: MediLink Legal <legal@medilink.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 16:12:00 +00:00
Subject: Questions on log retirement windows and subprocessor transfer clause

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the call earlier. Legal flagged two items we need clarified before we can sign the DPA addendum: 1) your team’s definition of ‘log retirement’ vs ‘backup purge’ (we want to be sure operational logs used for debugging are not kept longer than client data allowed) and 2) how Redwood handles subprocessors when a customer requests data transfer/escape-hatch (what happens to backup snapshots and cross-region copies).

Can you confirm:
- the timeline for primary log TTL vs backup snapshot deletion
- whether backups are automatically purged when a customer requests erasure or if they require a manual retention-override
- the contractual language Redwood proposes for subprocessor transfers so that we can map to our export controls

If you can send a short timeline and a proposed clause we can pass to our legal ops team. Appreciate it — Sara

--
Sara Cole
Head of Privacy & Compliance
MediLink Health
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Cole <sara.cole@medilink.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 17:03:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Questions on log retirement windows and subprocessor transfer clause

Hi Sara —

Thanks — captured below is our operational summary and an initial DPA appendix draft attached. High level: we separate three stores with independent lifecycles:

- App logs (service-level telemetry, structured traces): default TTL 30 days, retained for 90 days only when flagged for incident investigation.
- Customer data (the data you ingest via API): deletion/erase request triggers in-place deletion within 72 hours; KV caches and prefix caches are truncated immediately.
- Backups/snapshots (off-site, cross-region): default snapshot retention 90 days; snapshots are marked for purge after customer erase but not removed immediately — there is an escrow hold window.

Practical implications for MediLink: when you request a full erase under the DPA we will:
1) Delete customer data in primary stores within 72 hours.
2) Mark any backups/snapshots for purge; we schedule snapshot deletions during the next purge cycle (within 90 days) unless a short-cycle purge is requested and approved.
3) Allow a contractual carveout: for regulated customers we can offer an accelerated backup purge (30–45 days) for an additional compliance addendum and a subprocessor attestation.

Attached: redwood_log_retirement_timeline_v1.pdf (timeline + purge windows) and a first-pass DPA subprocessor appendix (DPA-subproc-appendix-draft.docx).

Kimberly and Laura — can you review the proposed subprocessor transfer clause (section 4.3 in the draft) and suggest language that covers escrow/escape-hatch and cross-border transfer notification?

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Cole <sara.cole@medilink.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:18:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Questions on log retirement windows and subprocessor transfer clause

Ben —

Skimming the draft, I redlined a few items and added a short clause for automatic purge triggers. Key points I changed:

- Added a defined term: "Snapshot Escrow Hold" (maximum 90 days unless accelerated in writing).
- If Customer requests Erasure, Redwood will mark snapshots and schedule deletions within 90 days. If Customer selects "Accelerated Purge" option we commit to 30–45 day deletion window and provide subprocessor attestations within 10 business days.
- For subprocessor transfers (temporary cross-border execution): Redwood will notify Customer within 5 business days and either perform cryptographic isolation of the customer partition or provide a temp subprocessor attestation; transfer may be reversed prior to purge if Customer requests.

I attached the redlines (sent to the Drive link) and left comment placeholders where we should offer MediLink a technical control (e.g., customer-managed KMS for snapshots) as a mitigation that often speeds sign-off.

Laura — can you drop the legal-approved fallback language for permanent purge timing? I kept room for a 45-day standard for EU regulated accounts.

K

--
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Cole <sara.cole@medilink.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 08:44:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Questions on log retirement windows and subprocessor transfer clause

Thanks, Kimberly — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- MediLink legal will accept a 45-day default snapshot purge for EU patient-data customers if we get subprocessor attestations and the option for an Accelerated Purge (30 days) as a paid compliance feature.
- We need explicit language that snapshots containing exported copies will not be used for analytics or model training (vendor lock). Please add a use restriction in section 4.4.
- On transfer notifications: 5 business days is acceptable but request that the notification includes the temporary subprocessor list and how long the processing will occur.

If you can send an updated appendix with those three items we’ll queue it for Legal review and try to close this week.

Best,
Sara

--
Sara Cole
Head of Privacy & Compliance
MediLink Health
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Cole <sara.cole@medilink.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 16:38:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Questions on log retirement windows and subprocessor transfer clause

Sara —

Thanks for the concrete responses. We updated the appendix and pushed a v2 to the Drive link (see related links). Summary of changes:
- Standard snapshot purge window for EU regulated accounts: 45 days.
- Accelerated Purge (30 days) available as an addendum; includes required subprocessor attestations delivered within 10 business days.
- Explicit prohibition on using retained snapshot material for model training or analytics was added to section 4.4.
- Transfer notification expanded to include temp subprocessor list and expected processing window; 5 business-day notice remains.

Next steps: Ben will include the updated timeline figure in the DPA exhibit and I will prepare the legal-approved final fallback text for section 4.3. If MediLink signs off, we can route for e-signature (DocuSign link included in related_links).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
